title: Real-Life Analogy: Planning a Travel Route

blocks.content: Real-Life Analogy: Planning a Travel Route
Assume you have to travel from city A to city F. In your travels, you might have to pass through other cities (B, C, D, E, etc.) before you reach your destination.
Here, each city has a unique predecessor and a unique successor. For example, city C has only one predecessor (city B) and one successor (city D).
Thus, linear data structures are a perfect solution for traveling from city A to city F.
However, in real life, the path won't be linear as shown in the image above.
There will be multiple paths to travel from A to F.
Because each city doesn't have a unique predecessor or successor, finding a path from A to F won't be optimal if we use a linear approach.
